Orlando Health provided five SPF 50 sunscreen stations throughout the stadium and IOA Plaza on Sept. 23 to help improve the fan experience.  Aryah Britt Knights football fans have dealt with the 81-degree average Orlando heat after five home games during the 2026 season at Acrisure Bounce House. To beat the heat, Orlando Health  provided five SPF 50 sunscreen stations throughout the stadium and IOA Plaza on Sept. 23, making the skin-protection product accessible during the hot football season. UCF athletics expressed their gratitude to Orlando Health for helping improve the fan experience. “Based on fan feedback from games played in the heat last season, we wanted to make sunscreen free and easy to access at Acrisure Bounce House this season,” UCF athletics said in a statement.  This is not the first time Orlando Health has partnered with UCF, as the healthcare organization supplied sunscreen stations to the stadium in prior seasons.  Ultima Espino, Orlando Health senior director of sports partnerships, said these are a second iteration of sunscreen stations placed at UCF athletic complexes previously, but aim to improve areas lacking in previous designs.  "A couple seasons back, there were different versions of the sunscreen stations and they just proved challenging to upkeep, believe it or not, in the Florida heat,” Espino said. "We forewent doing that for maybe the last season." Espino said the new stations are more advanced than previous models, providing information to Orlando Health about how often they're utilized. "These particular stations actually provide us with trackable data: how many usages and how many people utilized the station," Espino said. "So after the season, we'll have some of that data, which I think is very important and will show the benefit in a data-driven way." Espino said the university, during Acrisure Bounce House renovations, referred to spots in the stadium where fans bask under the sun more than others.  “When they re-did the stadium, UCF was mentioning there seem to be areas, even more so in this new stadium iteration, that have some direct sunlight,” Espino said. “With that, we were like, ‘What if we find a way to bring back the sunscreen stations and maybe it’s something we offer within the stadium?’” Espino said the sunscreen stations are placed around populated areas of Acrisure Bounce House: the east and west fan service areas, IOA Plaza and the stadium’s north side student gate. Knights fans first experienced the stations during UCF’s Big 12 Conference opener during its 21-13 victory against TCU on Sept. 26. Espino said Orlando Health plans to provide sunscreen stations at UCF sports facilities beyond Acrisure Bounce House. “We have committed to providing sunscreen stations at baseball and softball facilities because there is a high need and sun exposure there, so we will do that during baseball and softball season,” Espino said.  Until both seasons start in 2027, Knights fans can access the stations at the Bounce House for the remainder of home games during the football season.
